description:
FILED s526w2 (Opus, 2026-10-24), TT census.  LOUD for `${ ... }` (whole module refused: Template/Parser.pm:546 `(?: \{ ([^\}]*) \} )   # ${ ... }`); a plain `$x` in a comment is probably SILENT (interpolated into the pattern; not probed separately).

    print "2\n" if "q" =~ / q  # a comment naming ${ ... }
                       /x;
perl: 2.  PCL: Transpile failed: "PCL: cannot compile interpolated regex reference '${ ... }'".
toke.c scan_const skips a `#` comment to end of line when the pattern has /x and the `#` is outside a character class; the interpolation scanner (Pl/InterpScan.pm -- the only place, standing rule) must know the pattern's /x and do the same.  Reproducer scratch/s526w2/p4.pl.
Rows: every TT file that loads Template::Parser (counted when the TT census runs).
TT CENSUS (s526w2, resumed s528 2026-10-25): with #3855 fixed, Template::Parser is the ONE refusal left (Filters / Plugin::String / VMethods transpile now).  The board run of the dist: 3 PASS / 8 PARTIAL / 110 FAIL (121 files), 127 ok / 66 not ok; 98 files print no TAP (69 die, 29 TIMEOUT -> #3869), the rest are PERL-SKIPs perl also takes (Stash::XS x3, author / developer tests).  perl: 121 files, 3,144 tests, PASS.  Template-Toolkit does NOT join the board until this lands (a dist whose refusals stop every file is censused and does not join).  NOTE: docs/interp-scan.md lists //x #-comments as a deliberate v1 NON-GOAL of Pl/InterpScan.pm, so the fix lifts a recorded non-goal: the scanner needs the pattern's /x flag and character-class state (a # inside [...] is literal), at every in_regex caller (ExprToCL x3, VarAnnotator, Binder).

=== RULED s529 (Fable, 2026-10-29 00:4x): LIFT THE NON-GOAL -- toke.c's rule, in the ONE scanner, keyed on the TRAILING modifiers ===
The v1 non-goal (docs/interp-scan.md Â§12: `(?#...)` comments and //x `#`-comments scanned as plain text) is LIFTED: it is a real toke.c rule (S_scan_const: `#` outside a character class under RXf_PMf_EXTENDED copies to end of line uninterpolated; `(?#` outside a class copies to the next `)` uninterpolated), Template-Toolkit's 121 files sit behind it, and rule 4 (no easy write-offs) applies.  Probed perl 5.40.3 -> main (`~/pcl-agent-scratch/s529/probes/p3856[abc].pl`): main's divergences are (i) the LOUD refusal `${ ... }` in a comment (the filing), (ii) SILENT: a variable whose VALUE holds a newline ends the comment early (p3856c row 15: perl matches "q", main does not), (iii) SILENT with a SIDE EFFECT: `# calls @{[ f() ]}` runs f() on main, never in perl (row 16/17: calls=0 vs 1), (iv) `use re '/x'` (row 21): perl's lexer honours the pragma's flag and skips the comment; main interpolates.  Benign on main: a plain `$x` / `$h{k}` / `@nosuch` in a comment (the value lands inside the comment and the engine drops it; rows 2 and 10 pass).
THE RULE (one arm, one place -- standing rule Â§8, Pl/InterpScan.pm or not at all): `scan`/`scan_one` gain an option `x => 0|1` (the pattern's EXTENDED flag).  The scan loop keeps toke.c's `in_charclass` state (an unescaped `[` enters it, `]` leaves it, a backslash skips the next char -- toke.c's exact logic, no `[]...]` refinement: perl is the oracle and toke.c has none); with x set and not in a class, `#` skips to the end of the line; in any pattern not in a class, `(?#` skips to the next `)`; NO event is emitted inside a skipped region.  The flag comes from the OP'S TRAILING MODIFIERS only -- an inline `(?x)` does NOT count (row 14: perl interpolates there; main agrees today) -- so `x` is true for /x and /xx (row 12) and for qr//x (row 13); the s/// REPLACEMENT side is a string, never a pattern (row 11, unchanged).  Every in_regex caller passes it: Pl/ExprToCL.pm x3 (the Regexp token's modifiers are in hand), Pl/VarAnnotator.pm ~2100 (`$node->get_modifiers`), Pl/Binder.pm ~549 (its caller passes the token or the flag).  `use re '/x'` (row 21) is a SECOND SOURCE of the flag: if PCL tracks the `re` pragma's default flags for the engine, the same value feeds the scanner; if it does not, FILE that as its own task (engine + scanner together) and leave row 21 out of this guard -- say which in the commit.
GUARD (new file `Pl/t/regex-x-comment-01.t`, inverse-verified on main's code sha): the filing's `${ ... }` row; rows 15 (newline value), 16/17 (no side effect), 3/4/9 (a `#` inside `[...]` or escaped `\#` is NOT a comment -- the variable after it still interpolates), 5/6 (`(?#...)` with and without /x), 7/8 (no /x: `#` is literal and `$x` interpolates), 12 (/xx), 13 (qr), 14 (inline `(?x)` does not count), 11 (s/// replacement unaffected).  Records: docs/interp-scan.md Â§12 loses the two items and gains the rule as a contract line (charclass state is now TRACKED for this purpose only; the intuit_more classifier is unchanged); a DECIDED line; the TT census re-run afterwards (Template::Parser was the ONE refusal left after #3855 -- #3869's 29 hangs are behind it).
LAYER + SIZE: scanner only; the engine already handles /x comments (every row without a variable passes on main).  A filler-sized member of the next correctness batch (one mechanism, one guard file); NOT s526w2's (its batch is closing).

=== DONE (s529b, Opus, 2026-10-31) -- the RULED shape ===
Pl/InterpScan.pm: `scan` is now `_walk`, which also returns the COMMENT spans it skipped; `comment_spans()` exported for a consumer with its own name scan.  Option `x => 0|1`.  In a pattern (in_regex), outside a character class: `(?#` ... up to the next `)` (any pattern) and, with x, `#` ... up to the end of the line are skipped, no event inside.  in_charclass = toke.c S_scan_const's: an unescaped `[` enters, `]` leaves (backslash escapes already skip a char), no `[]...]` refinement -- AND it starts over after every interpolated variable, because scan_const RETURNS at a variable and is re-entered (probed perl 5.40.3: "ab" =~ /^[$x#]$y/x with $x="a", $y="b" does NOT match -- `#]$y` is a comment there; the guard's `cc` row).  The flag comes from the op's TRAILING modifiers: ExprToCL _regex_literal_form (m// qr//, from the flags string), gen_substitution_form (s///, $mods->{x}; the replacement is never scanned as a pattern), _regex_case_mod_pattern; Binder::_interp_refs (the token's get_modifiers); VarAnnotator::_tw_scan_quote_leaf (skips comment_spans over the PATTERN SECTION only -- never the delimiters, e.g. `m#...#`, or an s/// replacement).
`use re '/x'` (probe row 21): PCL does not track `use re '/FLAGS'` at all (engine included: `use re "/i"; "Q" =~ /q/` fails too) -> FILED #4042 (engine + scanner together); row 21 is not in the guard.
GUARD: Pl/t/regex-x-comment-01.t (23 rows = the 21-row probe set minus row 21, + `cc`/`cc2` for the class reset, + "both programs transpile whole"; the filing row runs as its own program so the others fail or pass on their own).  On main d8577478 the discriminating rows FAIL: 1-2 (the refusal), r15 (newline value), r17 (f() called), r19, cc; the benign rows pass on both.
CORPUS-DIFF vs 77c7d9d7: identical for this member (no corpus pattern has a variable in a comment).
ACCEPTANCE: `./pl2cl --module < ~/.cpan/build/Template-Toolkit-3.106-0/lib/Template/Parser.pm` exits 0, 1755 lines, 0 PARSE ERROR (it was the one TT refusal left after #3855).  NOTE for the TT census (not joined here, the next board batch's): a 6-line TT program (`Template->new->process(\"Hello [% name %]...")`) still fails at run time ("Can't call method process on unblessed reference") -- the census will find it.  Pod-Simple JustPod02.t (blessed to this task, *FILE* no TAP) passes 1/1 in a one-file run -> its row left baselines/cpan-board14-fails.tsv by edit.
docs/interp-scan.md §12: the two non-goal items removed, the contract line added; the InterpScan header updated.
subject: A `${ ... }` (or any variable) inside a /x regex COMMENT is interpolated by PCL -- perl skips # comments under /x before interpolation -- so Template::Parser refuses ("cannot compile interpolated regex reference ${ ... }")
